steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Advertising: paid communication through media channels (TV, radio, print, online, social media, billboards). It builds awareness and brand image but is expensive and difficult to measure ROI directly.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Sales promotion: short-term incentives to encourage purchase (BOGOF, discounts, coupons, free gifts, competitions). Boosts immediate sales but can damage brand image if overused.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Public relations (PR): managing the business's image through media coverage, press releases, events, and community involvement. It's credible (not paid for) but the business can't control the message.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Personal selling: one-to-one communication (sales reps, demonstrations). Effective for high-value, complex products but expensive per customer and limited reach.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Explain the difference between advertising and sales promotion, giving one advantage and one disadvantage of each. | Analyse why a business might choose social media marketing over traditional TV advertising. | Evaluate which promotional method would be most effective for a new luxury skincare brand targeting 25-35 year-old women.

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: Advertising: paid messages through media to build brand awareness and image. Advantage: reaches large audiences, builds long-term brand recognition. Disadvantage: expensive (TV adverts cost thousands) | Social media marketing advantages: highly targeted (demographics, interests, behaviours), lower cost than TV, interactive (customers can comment/share), measurable (clicks, conversions, engagement), b | For a luxury skincare brand targeting 25-35 women: social media/influencer marketing is most effective - this demographic spends significant time on Instagram and TikTok, follows beauty influencers, a

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Always match the promotional method to the TARGET MARKET: where do they spend time and who do they trust? When evaluating promotion, consider the BUDGET: small businesses can't afford TV but can afford social media. Remember the AIDA model: Awareness → Interest → Desire → Action. Different promotional methods work at different stages.
